statement: **Reconstructed from the reported title.** Return whether a string is a valid **decimal number**: an optional `+`/`-`, then digits with at most one `.`, and **at least one digit** (`"4."` and `"-.9"` are valid, `"."` is not). No spaces, no exponent.
provenance: "Restricted decimal number validator" in a LinkedIn phone screen (Sep 2026, FastPrep); the full version is LeetCode 65 Valid Number, which is LinkedIn-tagged. Only the title was reported, so the "restricted" grammar below is my reading — clarify it first.

stages.title: Restricted decimal
stages.say: Validate a decimal number: optional sign, digits, at most one dot.

stages.title: With an exponent
stages.say: Now accept exponents too: a decimal, then e or E and a signed integer.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe a small hand-written scanner — optional sign, digits, at most one dot, at least one digit — and the exponent version reuses it: split at the first e and require an integer after it. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Review, do not rewrite
prompts.text: Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it.

prompts.label: Race conditions
prompts.text: Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call IsDecimal concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet.

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs
prompts.text: Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct.

prompts.label: Complexity check
prompts.text: What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it.

prompts.label: Requirement change
prompts.text: The requirement changed: Add NumberValidator.IsNumber(s) (LeetCode 65). List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code.

learn.md:

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Parsers are clearest as "read the optional parts in order". Count digits instead of tracking states, and the only rule left is "at least one digit".

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy

- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- double.TryParse — culture, spaces and "NaN" make it accept invalid input.
- A regex nobody can review.
- Accepting "." or "+".
- Accepting two signs ("+-3").
